question: Of the two alfalfa silage groups, how many silos were in the group with the lower pH, and what acetic acid concentration did that group have?
rendered:
The document "Fermentation Quality Divergence of Alfalfa Silage within the Same Batch: Insights from 16S rRNA Sequencing and Untargeted Metabolomics" contains the answer.

From page 2, we can see that 49 silos were classified into the LPGood group (relatively well-fermented group) and 51 into the LPBad group (poorly fermented group).

From page 3, we can see that the LPGood group had a significantly lower pH value (5.10 ± 0.02) compared to the LPBad group (5.35 ± 0.04).

From page 3, we can also see that the LPGood group had a significantly higher acetic acid concentration (11.27 ± 0.16 g/kg DM) compared to the LPBad group (10.01 ± 0.81 g/kg DM).

So, the answer is: there were 49 silos in the group with the lower pH (LPGood group), and that group had an acetic acid concentration of 11.27 ± 0.16 g/kg DM.
